'''Cody Leron Williams''' (born November 20, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class. He is the younger brother of [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] player [[Jalen Williams]].

==Early life==

web|url=https://www.eastvalleytribune.com/sports/cody-williams-becoming-star-for-perry-basketball/article_5df7f244-7ab1-11eb-a9b6-abb2ecf7747f.html|title=Cody Williams becoming star for Perry basketball|first=Zach|last=Alvira|work=[[East Valley Tribune]]|date=March 1, 2021|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> As a junior, Williams was named the Premier Region Player of the Year after with Colorado|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|date=November 9, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite |work=[[MaxPreps.com]]}}</ref>
Williams was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2023/01/25/baye-fall-cody-williams-mcdonalds-all-americans/|title=Colorado’s Baye Fall, CU Buffs recruit Cody Williams named McDonald’s All Americans|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> He was also selected to play for Team USA in the [[Nike Hoops Summit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://colorado.rivals.com/news/colorado-signee-cody-williams-named-to-team-usa-roster-for-nike-hoop-summit|title=Colorado signee Cody Williams named to Team USA roster for Nike Hoop Summit|first=Craig|last=Meyer|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=February 15, 2023|archive-date=May 12, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230512004338/https://colorado.rivals.com/news/colorado-signee-cody-williams-named-to-team-usa-roster-for-nike-hoop-summit|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Williams was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class, according to major recruiting services.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |date=August 29, 2022 |title=Arizona target Cody Williams rises to No. 14 in ESPN class of 2023 rankings |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-target-cody-williams-rises-to-no-14-in-espn-class-of-2023-rankings/article_e65bf24c-27bd-11ed-8f23-c7d27f99ab52.html |access-date=February 1, 2023 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/College-basketball-recruiting-top-25-Cody-Williams-discusses-final-eight-Arizona-Colorado-Georgia-Tech-LMU-LSU-Santa-Clara-UCLA-USC-193333815/|title=Top 25 senior Cody Williams updates his recruitment in the midst of visits|first=Eric|last=Bossi|website=[[247Sports]]|date=September 13, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> On November 9, 2022, Williams committed to playing college basketball for [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] after considering offers from [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34986747/colorado-lands-first-five-star-recruit-tad-boyle-tenure|title=Colorado lands first five-star recruit of Tad Boyle's tenure|first1=Jeff|last1=Borzello|first2=Paul|last2=Biancardi|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 9, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> He became the highest-ranked committed recruit in program history and the first five-star recruit to join Colorado.

==College career==
As a freshman, Williams averaged 11.9 points and 3.0 rebounds per game, helping the Buffaloes earn a berth in the NCAA Tournament. He was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team. Following the season Williams declared for the 2024 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite news |title=Forward Cody Williams declares for the NBA draft after a single season at Colorado |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-basketball/news/forward-cody-williams-declares-for-the-nba-draft-after-a-single-season-at-colorado |access-date=December 8, 2024 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 22, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 26, 2024, Williams was selected with the tenth overall pick by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2024 NBA Draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Larsen|title=Utah Jazz draft Colorado forward Cody Williams at No. 10 in NBA Draft|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2024/06/26/utah-jazz-draft-colorado-forward/|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 26, 2024}}</ref> and on July 2, he signed with them.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Cody Williams and Isaiah Collier|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-cody-williams-and-isaiah-collier|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}}</ref> Throughout his rookie season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Salt Lake City Stars Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Salt-Lake-City-Stars/42/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 18, 2024}}</ref> In his rookie season, Williams averaged 4.6 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cody Williams Stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4895758/cody-williams |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 13, 2026}}</ref>

Entering the 2025−26 season, Williams began to see an increase in minutes, and in his increased role, he began to see some signs of improvement.<ref>{{cite web |last=Koch |first=Jared |title=Utah Jazz's Cody Williams Sets Clear Goal for Year Two |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/onsi/news/utah-jazz-cody-williams-sets-clear-goal-year-two |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 6, 2025 |access-date=January 13, 2026}}</ref> In the 2025−26 season, Williams also saw his first-ever start, where in the games against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], he scored eight points, tallied four rebounds, and dished out two steals in 22 minutes of gameplay.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jazz's Cody Williams: Sees 22 minutes in start |url=https://www.rotowire.com/basketball/headlines/cody-williams-news-sees-22-minutes-in-start-512697 |website=Rotowire via CBS Sports |access-date=January 13, 2026}}</ref> On Saturday, January 10, 2026, in a demoralizing blow against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], Williams finished the game with a −60, making it the worst [[Plus–minus (sports)|+/−]] record in NBA history, beating both [[Scoot Henderson]]'s and [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]]'s record of −58.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wimbish |first=Jasmyn |title=How historic was the Hornets' beatdown of the Jazz? This one stat shows just how eye-popping the win was |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/how-historic-was-the-hornets-beatdown-of-the-jazz-this-one-stat-shows-just-how-eye-popping-the-win-was/ |newspaper=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 11, 2026 |access-date=January 14, 2026}}</ref> On March 15, Williams recorded a career-high 34 points with seven rebounds in a 111–113 loss to the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jazz’s Cody Williams: Erupts for career-high 34 in loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-cody-williams-erupts-for-career-high-34-in-loss/|access-date=May 10, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

On August 29, 2026, Williams and [[John Konchar]] were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]], and cash considerations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Forwards John Konchar and Cody Williams from Utah Jazz {{!}} Minnesota Timberwolves |url=https://timberwolves.com/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-forwards-john-konchar-and-cody-williams-from-utah-jazz |access-date=2026-08-29 |website=timberwolves.com |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Williams was named to the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-19 basketball team]], which was coached by Colorado head coach [[Tad Boyle]], to play in the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/colorado/article/colorado-basketball-buffaloes-forward-cody-williams-makes-2023-u-211662556/|title=Cody Williams makes the 2023 USA U19 men's national team|first=Adam|last=Munsterteiger|website=[[247Sports]]|date=June 16, 2023|access-date=June 21, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Williams is the son of Ron and Nicole Williams. He has two older siblings, Jasmine and Jalen.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cody Williams - Men's Basketball |url=https://cubuffs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/cody-williams/16572 |website=University of Colorado Athletics |access-date=26 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Williams' older brother, [[Jalen Williams]], currently plays for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the [[National Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |date=June 19, 2022 |title=While Jalen Williams is talk of NBA Draft, younger brother Cody draws Arizona's attention |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/while-jalen-williams-is-talk-of-nba-draft-younger-brother-cody-draws-arizonas-attention/article_21cd21f8-eeb5-11ec-a337-43852f721c62.html |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]]}}</ref>
